questions.q: Choose the correct inversion of: “If I had known about the problem, I would have helped you.”
opts: Had I known about the problem, I would have helped you.
Have I known about the problem, I would have helped you.
Did I know about the problem, I would have helped you.
Were I known about the problem, I would have helped you.
questions.why: Third conditional inverts to 'Had + subject + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The doctor asked him to ______ smoking.”
questions.why: Give up = stop doing; give in = surrender. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “If she had taken the medicine on time, she ____ better now.”
questions.why: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “A person who is gradually recovering health after illness”
questions.why: A convalescent is someone regaining health after sickness. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: “Open the door, ____?”
questions.why: An imperative takes 'will you' as its tag. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: “Not a single word ____ during the interview.”
questions.why: Negative object phrase in front requires did + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: He said, “I am busy today.”
opts: He said that he was busy that day.
He said that I am busy today.
He said that he is busy today.
He said that he had been busy today.
questions.why: Present becomes past; 'today' becomes 'that day'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “His explanation was deliberately ____ to avoid responsibility.”
questions.why: Ambiguous: open to more than one meaning. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2026.

questions.q: Change into passive voice: “Who wrote this letter?”
opts: By whom was this letter written?
By whom this letter was written?
Whom was this letter written by him?
questions.why: 'Who' becomes 'By whom' + was + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “Although he is rich, but he is not happy.”
questions.why: 'Although' and 'but' must not be used together. GPSC-style practice item.
